name: Mad Professor
hook: A Guyanese electronics repairman in south London built his own mixing desk and carried Tubby-style dub into a second generation and a second country.
blurb: Neil Fraser, known as Mad Professor, moved from Guyana to London at thirteen and worked repairing electronics before building his own mixing board. In 1979 he opened Ariwa, a four-track studio in his living room, and used it to carry on the version-and-echo tradition King Tubby and Lee Perry had built in Kingston, now from London. He stands for dub's move abroad, into Britain's Jamaican community, still made on self-built equipment rather than in commercial studios, the same conditions that shaped the original Kingston scene. His work later crossed out of reggae, including a 1995 dub remix of Massive Attack's 'Protection', which carried dub's structure straight into trip-hop.

signatureTracks.title: Dub Me Crazy! The Beginning of a New Cult
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The first release in Mad Professor's long-running Dub Me Crazy series, and the record that established Ariwa's house sound.

signatureTracks.title: No Protection
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A full dub remix of Massive Attack's 'Protection' album, carrying King Tubby's structural logic directly into 1990s trip-hop.
